newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota wheat harvest advances rapidly.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota wheat harvest advances rapidly.

text.p: Hot, dry weather allowed harvesting of North Dakota's spring wheat crop to advance rapidly during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
But the heat and dryness meant that condition ratings declined for all crops except spring wheat, oats and potatoes.

Forty-one percent of the spring wheat acreage was combined, a marked improvement over 21 last week and 29 last year and roughly on par with the average of 42 percent. The spring wheat crop was rated 60 percent good to excellent, 31 fair and nine percent poor to very poor.
Percentage condition for other small grains was as follows (from good to poor): durum, 51, 35, and 14; oats 64, 31 and five; barley 68, 25 and seven.

Twenty percent of the state's durum was combined, compared to 13 percent last year and the average of 25 percent. Fifty-three percent of the barley was combined, ahead of 42 percent last year but lagging the average of 62 percent.
Soil mositure conditions declined, leaving late-season crops like corn, dry beans and soybeans in need of rain.
Pasture and range conditions increased and were rated 47 percent good to excellent, 37 fair and 14 poor to very poor.
